title: Nested VRUN, enhanced for the SNES (shaded sprites and blocks, custom font)
description: The Nested VRUN ROM with the 'a notch above the NES' graphics pass (tools/snes_enhance.py, a post-build tool; the pinned core is untouched): a custom 16-colour text font, and hue-shifted bevel shading (warm highlights, cool shadows) on sprites and room art, using the 12 SNES palette entries per palette that a NES-recompiled game never touches. The shading planes are uploaded in the NMI; they follow the displayed CHR bank.

toolchain: BrokenNes Workshop --brokendev dump-chr (replaces the Mesen CHR dump the tool's header describes)

steps.name: dump-chr
steps.note: The game's CHR RAM (all four 8 KB banks) after 600 frames of the title, as the NES version uploads it. snes_enhance.py reads it to know the tile art (bank 0 = room art + font + sprites, bank 1 = the same art shifted one tile, bank 2 = title logo + font).

steps.name: enhance
steps.note: Command as recorded in the Nested notes (v2): --full-bevel-from 64 shades tiles 64 and up fully (objects and blocks), walls below it keep their dominant colour; animated tiles (found by matching src/game/anim_*.png) are skipped.

run.note: Same game and controls as Nested VRUN; the picture has shaded sprites and blocks and a different font.

oracle.why: As vrun-nested (input shift 1). Until 2026-10-23 the enhanced ROM needed shift 4: its boot uploads of 2 KB shading planes split Nested's title-start catch-up of NES frames differently on the two emulators (BrokenNes 2+2, Mesen 3+1). Project Nested f13a2f9 holds the uploads until rendering has been on once; since then the catch-up is +4 in one frame on both and the diff is pixel-identical at shift 1.

compat.what: As vrun-nested (the enhancement is a post-build pass on that ROM: the same NES build, so vrun-nested's .mlb names the variables).

scenarios.what: power-on, the title, Start, verify's play script

checks.what: boots to the title (app_state 0 before Start)
the title runs (the NES NMI counter ticks)
the title looks like BrokenNes' title
the scripted play stays in the game
the game keeps running to the end (the NES NMI counter keeps ticking)
gameplay is drawn at the end

scenarios.what: as vrun-nested: Start, pause, Select = save and quit into the SRAM-emulated flash

checks.what: save and quit returns to the title
the title cursor lands on CONTINUE (title_cursor 1)

scenarios.what: a fresh boot of the same emulator with the SRAM of 'save'

checks.what: a fresh boot finds the save (save_exists 1: CONTINUE is offered)
BrokenDev hardware checks (docs/projects/brokendev-debugging-plan.md, D4): every verify scenario runs again with the checks on; a finding not accepted here fails verify. Each acceptance says why.

accepted.reason: known: Project Nested runs the NES game's frame across the SNES vblank and cannot reproduce NES lag frames (knownIssues); the boot's recompile and loading frames lag

known: the nested engine's reset does ROL $420D: MEMSEL is write-only, so the read is open bus and the FastROM bit it writes back depends on the open-bus value ($42 on hardware, the operand's high byte, which turns FastROM on); harmless on hardware, worth a plain STA in the engine
unverified: the nested runtime reads INIDISP ($2100, write-only: open bus) once in play (frame 246, pc $C23809); to look at in Project Nested

budgets.what: Over a limit fails verify, near it (90%) warns; the report compares with the previous build (out/<id>/budget-history.json). romBankFree is an estimate (padding runs of 64 or more equal $00 / $FF bytes).

lagFrames.what: with the engine's frame wait declared ($80A739): 0 on 2026-10-24

knownIssues: The enhancement is keyed to the game's tile layout (tile numbers in the CHR dump and src/game/anim_*.png): a change to VRUN's art needs a fresh dump and may need the tile ranges in the command revisited.
The pass uses WRAM $7E:10DA-10DF and ROM space in banks $81 and $C2 that the pinned core leaves free; a later core step that claims that space would collide (core/SPACE.md is the registry).
Same Nested limits as vrun-nested: no NES lag-frame emulation, no entry-point feedback in this recipe.
